chapters.title: Prologue
chapters.intro: A short, scripted opening. There's nothing to miss here, so enjoy it.

chapters.title: Just Like Paradise
chapters.intro: Island life in the Keys. Most of the game's permanent missables live in this chapter, almost all of them around Jason's house. Settle in, poke around the swamps and don't rush the ending.

chapters.title: Paradise Lost
chapters.intro: A fresh start somewhere less glamorous. One mid-chapter mission opens up switching and a burst of side content. The mountains are worth the drive.

chapters.title: Tits Ass Drug Money
chapters.intro: The city opens up. Robbery systems, street racing and a lot of side characters arrive. One timed race, one choice with a follow-up and two in-mission pickups need attention.

chapters.title: Vice City, Baby
chapters.intro: A long heist arc with a stretch where the two leads can't be seen together. Two side missions can be lost, so watch the warnings.

coverage.note: The first half is well documented. Late missions, and exactly what the end of the chapter closes off, are still thin.

chapters.title: Top of the World, Ma
chapters.intro: The finale. Endings are reported to depend on choices, relationship, criminal profiles and money. Mission names here are hidden by default.

coverage.note: The least documented chapter so far. Mission order, side content and missables may change as guides catch up.

chapters.title: After the Credits
chapters.intro: Free roam continues and the 100% checklist unlocks. Nothing on it can be missed. Take your time.

coverage.note: Collectible maps and totals are still being confirmed.

activities.title: Set up the game for a completionist run
activities.spoilerFreeDescription: Turn on every progress and collectible notification under Settings > UI, including Criminal Profile updates. You'll get a quiet ping whenever something counts.
activities.whyNow: Costs a minute and means you never wonder whether a find registered.

activities.title: Prologue
activities.spoilerFreeDescription: The game's opening. Basic on-foot controls and a scripted chase. Nothing in the Prologue can be missed.
activities.whyNow: There's no free roam yet. Play it straight; the outcome is scripted, so don't hunt for a better route.

activities.title: Make a permanent chapter-entry save
activities.spoilerFreeDescription: You get 15 manual save slots plus one autosave. There's no mission replay and no New Game+, so keep one slot for the start of every chapter and never overwrite it.
activities.whyNow: Guides agree this is the single best protection against missing anything.

activities.title: Gone Fishing
unlocks: Jason's Key Lento house: wardrobe, cash stash, deck gym, TV
activities.spoilerFreeDescription: Your first real outing in the Keys. Completing it gives you Jason's Key Lento house (wardrobe, cash stash, deck gym, TV) plus binoculars and a flashlight.
activities.whyNow: Opens your home base and the binoculars you'll use for wildlife study all game. Watch for loose cash during the mission.

fight.note: Stealth works for part of it.

activities.title: Spare cash on the way out

missable.warning: Inside this mission only. If you finish the mission without it, it's gone for good.

activities.spoilerFreeDescription: During your first swamp job there's money lying around that you can't come back for once the mission ends.
activities.whyNow: One-time pickup inside a mission. Once you're airborne it's gone.
hints: While you're out in the swamp on this job, keep your eyes open. There's money nobody is guarding.
Someone mentions it in passing. It's on the route back to the plane.
Look inside the red-and-white trailer at the swamp camp before you board.
Cash sits in the red-and-white trailer at the Kingfisher camp in the Pelican Valley swamp; Donnie mentions it. Grab it on the way to the plane. The amount isn't documented.

activities.title: Know how your criminal profile works
activities.spoilerFreeDescription: Every character builds a criminal profile from how you play. Limb shots and stealth lean Professional; kills lean Psycho. Reaching Irredeemable is permanent for that character, and the ending is reported to consider your profile.
activities.whyNow: Easier to steer from the start than to fix later. If you want every option open at the end, stay below Irredeemable.
activities.notes: PC Gamer, quoted in project research: once you have an Irredeemable profile, it's permanent. How much the profile affects the ending is reported but not fully documented.

activities.title: Start studying wildlife with binoculars
activities.spoilerFreeDescription: Study animals you come across with the binoculars. 100% needs 100 of 255, and every dog and cat breed counts separately.
activities.whyNow: Free and passive. It piles up over 60 to 80 hours if you start now, so there's no grind later.

activities.title: Reading material around the house

missable.warning: These spots are lost when you leave the house for good at the end of Chapter 1. Other copies exist, so the 100% magazine count is still reachable.

activities.spoilerFreeDescription: Jason's house has several things to read, inside and out. These spots won't be reachable after this chapter. Copies exist elsewhere for the magazine total, but this is the easy moment.
activities.whyNow: The house is your base for all of Chapter 1 and then it's gone. Five quick pickups now save a hunt later.
hints: Take a slow lap of the house. Reading material turns up inside, below and out back.
Check the bedroom, the living room, a table by a window, the shed under the house and the back deck.
Bedside table; living-room table; table by the east window; workbench in the shed under the house; back deck by the weights.

Ashes of Glory (bedside table), Lethal by Design (living-room table; a Liberty City memoir, a GTA IV nod), Orca: A Whole Different Animal (table by the east window), Off the Hook (shed workbench; it also marks fishing hotspots on your map) and Body Copy (back deck by the weights). Magazines count toward 30 of 34 for 100%.

activities.title: Look closely at the yard and the TV
activities.spoilerFreeDescription: Jason's place hides a couple of nods for long-time fans of the series. Small, but you won't be able to look for them after this chapter.
activities.whyNow: Environmental storytelling, and the house won't be accessible after Chapter 1.
hints: Jason's house has a couple of little winks for series fans.
One is outside in the yard. The other plays on screen indoors.
Check the navigation screen on the boat in the yard. Leave the TV on for a while.
The boat's GPS in Jason's yard shows a map of Los Santos (GTA V). A Weazel News report about the skunk ape plays on the TV.

activities.title: Gear Up
activities.safeTitle: A trip to the gun store
activities.spoilerFreeDescription: Opens Ammu-Nation and longarms. Body armor and a parachute are on sale at the Key Lento Ammu-Nation.
activities.whyNow: Exploration in the swamps gets dangerous. You want armor and a rifle before you go looking for the good stuff.
activities.notes: Ultimate Edition: Jason's engraved Girardi ES9 appears in the weapon locker after this mission (Output Lag).

fight.note: Fighting is optional.

activities.title: Lab Fees
activities.spoilerFreeDescription: Introduces the duffel bag and your first fence.
activities.whyNow: You'll be picking up valuables from now on. This gives you somewhere to carry and sell them.

fight.note: Talking can avoid it.

activities.title: Just a Scratch
activities.spoilerFreeDescription: Repairs and resprays at Coastal Auto Care. The mechanic will also bring your car to you during Chapter 1.
activities.whyNow: Quick, and car delivery saves a lot of walking in the Keys.

activities.title: Unwanted Attention
activities.spoilerFreeDescription: Adds the police scanner app. Most guides also place the WAiNK scanning app here.
activities.whyNow: WAiNK scanning (vehicles, landmarks) is the cheapest long-term progress in the game. Start it early.
activities.notes: Conflict: one guide delays the full WAiNK tutorial to Chapter 2's Moses.

fight.note: Stealth works.

activities.title: Start scanning vehicles with WAiNK
activities.spoilerFreeDescription: Hold Up on the D-pad, then R1/RB, to scan vehicles. 100% needs 200 of 277 base models. Boats and aircraft count too. Landmarks you scan count toward a separate 100-location target.
activities.whyNow: It's free while you drive around anyway. Starting now means you'll hit 200 naturally.
activities.notes: Unlock point is disputed (Unwanted Attention vs Moses in Chapter 2). The 200 of 277 requirement is consistent across sources; one page also cites 557 including variants.

activities.title: Keep an eye out for flamingos, cards and hoops
activities.spoilerFreeDescription: Three long-running collections start now: special flamingos (only those with a black-and-white beak count; 100 of 125), collectible cards (15 of 18 sets) and basketball hoops (90 of 100). Grab them when you pass them; don't hunt yet.
activities.whyNow: None of these can be missed and none are needed now. Noticing them early just makes cleanup shorter.

activities.title: The outpost in the swamp
activities.spoilerFreeDescription: Deep in the swamp country, an abandoned outpost is hiding more than it lets on. Bring patience and a curious mind. There's a unique reward, and something guarding it.
activities.whyNow: Reachable in the first hours of Chapter 1 and one of the best early finds. It turns a quiet swamp trip into a small mystery.
hints: Head into the Pelican Valley swamp. Somewhere out there, a cluster of old shacks has a story to tell.
Look for an abandoned research outpost: a main building and several shacks. Power is the first problem to solve.
Restore power at the electrical box behind the main building. The floorboards hold a password, a computer and a safe hold the rest, and the first shack's keypad door is the goal.

Switch on the electrical box at the back of the main building; examine the floorboards for passwords; log into the PC with CLEAVES (the buttons shuffle); a giant crab attacks when you back out of the PC; open the safe next to the PC with 0072; the first shack's keypad door code is 0212. Inside: the Crabshack VF5 (unique Vom Feuer VF5 SMG) and a stash bag of marked bills.
activities.notes: Output Lag and Detonated agree on the weapon and the outpost. GTA6 GPS has a pin labelled 'crab gun' that likely matches.

activities.title: A cabin nobody came back from
activities.region: Pelican Valley swamp, southwest of Hamlet
activities.spoilerFreeDescription: Somewhere in the wetlands, a wrecked cabin tells a grim story. Two unique rewards wait for anyone willing to wade in. No fight, but the water isn't friendly.
activities.whyNow: Two unique finds in one stop, both available now, and a strong bit of environmental storytelling.
hints: The swamps west of Hamlet hide a place that went very wrong for someone. It's worth the wade.
Southwest of Hamlet, in the middle of the Pelican Valley swamp. Watch the water on the way in.
Find the wrecked cabin in the middle of the swamp. Search the main room, including its far side.
Swamp Bait Akulus Revolver lies on the blood-covered floor in the middle of the room. Cruel Huntsman's SM-69 sniper rifle sits on the far side with sniper ammo. No enemies inside.
activities.notes: Output Lag, Detonated and Sportskeeda's summary all place both weapons in the Pelican Valley marsh southwest of Hamlet.

activities.title: The island Donnie talks about
activities.spoilerFreeDescription: Remember the island someone mentioned early on? The crew who holds it keeps something worth taking. Expect heavy resistance.
activities.whyNow: A unique reward that rewards preparation. Do it once you have armor and a longarm.
hints: An island mentioned in passing early in the chapter is home to a rival crew, and they keep something special.
Approach by boat. The prize is inside their fishing shack.
Clear the armed crew at the Kingfishers' fishing shack and open the weapon case inside.

Kingfishers W-22 small game rifle (comes with scope and suppressor) in a weapon case inside the Kingfishers' fishing shack on the island Donnie mentions. Detonated and Space4Games place the shacks in Wetman Bay; one map pins it in Mariana County. A big armed crew guards it; bring armor.

activities.title: The run-down motel south of Hamlet

missable.warning: Unconfirmed: one guide says driving off to lose the police can board up the room for good. Save before entering.

activities.spoilerFreeDescription: A tired roadside motel has more going on in its rooms than it should. A unique reward is inside, but it may not stay accessible if you leave in a hurry.
activities.whyNow: Available now. Save before you go in, because one report says the rooms can board up for good.
hints: A motel on the road south of Hamlet, with a striped mascot out front, is worth a closer look.
Loot the first room, then check the room next door. Expect company.
The prize is in the second room. A second crew arrives and the police may follow. Finish inside before you flee.

Kingfishers Laird 350 sporting sniper rifle, in the second room of the run-down tiger motel south of Hamlet. A second crew arrives; cops may follow. If you drive off to lose the cops, the room may board up and stay shut.
activities.notes: Output Lag places it south of Hamlet; GTA6 GPS has a 'Kingfisher Laird 350' pin in a different region. Boarding-up risk is single-source. Detonated lists the same rifle at the Manatee Motel in Gullet Marsh, as an illegal operation. That may or may not be the same motel.

activities.title: Gunshots on a country road
activities.spoilerFreeDescription: If you hear gunfire on the rural roads, don't drive away. Helping a stranger can pay off in a unique way.
activities.whyNow: A random encounter, so it can't be scheduled. Just keep this in mind while you're out exploring.
hints: Out on quiet country roads, gunfire isn't always a threat. Sometimes it's a call for help.
Follow gunshots near dirt roads in the countryside.
Two men by a dirt road, one of them wounded. Offer to help and get him to medical care fast.
Drive the wounded hunter to the hospital in his own truck; he hands you the Hunter's Laird 350 sporting sniper rifle. Random encounter; location isn't fixed.
activities.notes: Detonated (Nov 20) lists this rifle but hadn't found where it comes from.

activities.title: Stranded at sea
activities.spoilerFreeDescription: Getting stuck far out at sea isn't always a disaster. Someone unexpected might come to the rescue.
activities.whyNow: Pure delight, and there's something worth finding at the end. Try it any time you have a boat or jet ski.
hints: If you ever find yourself stranded far from shore, wait. Help may arrive in an unusual form.
Get stranded out on the open water rather than swimming back.
A rescuer on a jet ski can take you somewhere you wouldn't otherwise find. Look around when you arrive.
When stranded at sea, a dog on a jet ski picks you up and carries you to an island full of dogs. A hidden wallet with $1,218 is reported there. Exact trigger conditions aren't fully documented.

activities.title: Pipework
activities.spoilerFreeDescription: A rent collection that needs the four earlier jobs done first. Watch the floor before you leave.
activities.whyNow: Unlocks the next stretch of side content, including the neighbor's errands.

activities.title: Something dropped during the rent call

missable.warning: Only available during this mission.

activities.spoilerFreeDescription: During this rent collection, the tenant drops something you might want to keep. You can't come back for it.
activities.whyNow: One-time pickup inside a mission.
hints: Something small changes hands during this visit. Keep your eyes down.
Check the floor before you leave the house.
The tenant tosses something on the floor. Pick it up before walking out.
Mandy throws a Macizo cigar on the floor. Pick it up before leaving her house. Its use isn't documented.

activities.title: Help the neighbor (part 1)
activities.region: Key Lento, next to Jason's house

missable.earliest: After the first four Key Lento jobs
missable.warning: Both neighbor errands vanish once Tourist Trap starts. Not needed for trophies or 100%, but you won't see them again.

activities.spoilerFreeDescription: Jason's neighbor could use a hand. Small errands, but they disappear for good once the chapter's endgame starts.
activities.whyNow: Permanently missable and right next door. Do both parts now while you're living here.
hints: The neighbor next door has a small favor to ask.
Look for her marker right by Jason's place in Key Lento.
Talk to Shirley next door. The first errand is a supply run to a store.

Get Shirley's Rum. A hidden stash of about $1,300 is reported in a parrot cage during this errand. One guide adds that asking the clerk about bird noises reveals an Exotic Animals Front activity. Followed by Steal the Scooter.

activities.title: Help the neighbor (part 2)

missable.warning: Vanishes once Tourist Trap starts.

activities.spoilerFreeDescription: The neighbor's second, final errand.
activities.whyNow: Same deadline as part 1.
hints: Shirley has one more thing she needs.
Her second errand starts from the same spot.
It involves a set of wheels that isn't yours.
Steal the Scooter. Reward isn't documented. Neither Shirley errand counts toward Strangers & Freaks.

activities.title: Hey Arnold!
activities.spoilerFreeDescription: Contains a choice. Guides disagree on its weight: one says it's logged permanently on your criminal profile; another says it creates no story branch.
activities.whyNow: Next on the path. Save first.
activities.notes: Choice: kill or spare Arnold (Output Lag: recorded on criminal profile; Dork: no story branch).

gate.title: A choice is coming
gate.warning: This mission contains a choice that may be logged on your criminal profile. There's no mission replay.
gate.save: Make a manual save before you start, so you can live with your decision or reload.

fight.note: You'll shoot from a vehicle.

activities.title: Island Dreams
activities.spoilerFreeDescription: Introduces diving, treasure hunting and the metal detector.
activities.whyNow: Opens an entire treasure-hunting questline and the metal detector. Big exploration value.

activities.title: Treasure dives with Kenton
activities.spoilerFreeDescription: Kenton has more dives for you a little while after your first one. It's a long treasure-hunting chain across several shipwrecks, with underwater discoveries along the way.
activities.whyNow: Start it now. He goes quiet after Chapter 1 and returns later, so nothing is lost, but the first sets are here in the Keys.
hints: After your first dive, give it some time. Kenton will want you back.
Look for a green 'KR' icon in Key Lento.
Each set is a shipwreck with several underwater discoveries. The metal detector helps.

7 shipwreck sets in total; 100% needs 5 of 7 sets plus all 33 underwater discoveries. Kenton pauses after Chapter 1 and returns between Chapters 2 and 3 (calling Brian as Jason reportedly speeds it up). Not missable.
activities.notes: Sources disagree on the 100% requirement (PowerPyx: 5 of 7 sets; Game-Checklists: all 7). A Kenton trophy ('This Was No Boat Accident') appears in project research, but PowerPyx's trophy list doesn't show a Kenton trophy. Unconfirmed.

activities.title: Feng Shui
activities.spoilerFreeDescription: Unlocks the home console games. Afterwards, a set of errands for Lucia appears; they only count before the next story mission.
activities.whyNow: The errands it opens set your starting relationship level. Stop after this mission and do them.

activities.title: Get ready for Lucia's return

missable.warning: These errands only count before Coming Home. After that, the chance to set the starting relationship level is gone.

activities.spoilerFreeDescription: A handful of small errands appear: groceries, flowers, a gift, a haircut and some clothes. They only count before the next story mission, and together they set your starting relationship level.
activities.whyNow: Relationship level is reported to feed into the ending. These are quick and they expire at the next mission.
hints: Someone's coming home soon. A few thoughtful errands around Key Lento will make a difference.
Check the map after Feng Shui for small purple errand markers around Key Lento.
Groceries (pick up and drop off), flowers, a necklace, a haircut and clothes from a friend.

Pick Up / Drop Off Groceries, Buy Flowers, Buy Lucia a Necklace (The Siren's Chest), Get The Chop (Barnacle Beauties), Get Lucia's Clothes (from Andy at the Manatee's Rest). They count only before Coming Home. The necklace has a small follow-up early in Chapter 2.

activities.title: Fix up the house

missable.warning: Repairs count toward the relationship only before Coming Home.

activities.spoilerFreeDescription: The house needs a little work: the roof and a bedroom wall. It counts toward getting ready for Lucia.
activities.whyNow: Counts before Coming Home, and the house is lost at the end of the chapter.
hints: The house isn't quite ready for a guest.
Look up, and look at the bedroom walls.
Interact with the damaged roof tiles and the bedroom plasterboard.
Fix the roof tiles and the bedroom plasterboard. One guide says repairs count only before Coming Home; another lists them as a before-Tourist-Trap task.

activities.title: A fishing challenge from Cal
activities.spoilerFreeDescription: Cal sends a friendly challenge a little while after Feng Shui. A relaxed fishing outing with a trophy attached.
activities.whyNow: Fishing is open from free roam already, and this is a gentle way into it.
hints: Cal thinks he can out-fish you. Wait for his text.
The challenge is in Gambit Bay.
You need a specific species above a certain weight. The Off the Hook magazine in Jason's shed marks hotspots.
Catch a Bigger Fish: a stoplight parrotfish over 2 lb in Gambit Bay. Earns Baited My Tackle.

activities.title: Play the games on Jason's TV
activities.spoilerFreeDescription: Jason's TV has three playable games. They count toward 100% and the Master of None trophy. They're unavailable for most of Chapter 2 and come back in Chapter 3.
activities.whyNow: A cozy break between jobs. Not permanently missable.
activities.notes: Games: Tenebrae Lux, Street Trash III, Time Jackers Rewind. The fourth for 100% (Bang For Your Buck) is on arcade machines.

activities.title: Coming Home
activities.spoilerFreeDescription: Closes the window for Lucia's pre-release errands and house repairs.
activities.whyNow: Only start it once the errands are done.

activities.title: Clean Up After Donnie
activities.spoilerFreeDescription: Can be played before or after the next mission. Opens Donnie's drop-off for selling narcotics at better rates.
activities.whyNow: Unlocks a better narcotics fence that disappears later in the chapter.

fight.note: Cover is scarce, so keep healing items handy.

activities.title: Buck Me
activities.spoilerFreeDescription: Sets up BuckMe banking and Family Savings. Family Savings can't be withdrawn, but it raises limits and gives perks.
activities.whyNow: Banking is how money survives the end of this chapter.
activities.notes: One report places the RydeMe fast-travel app here; another says after Chapter 2. Until then, taxis go anywhere for about $100.

activities.title: Bank your money

missable.warning: Pocket cash, the floor stash and anything not in Family Savings won't carry over past Tourist Trap. Sources disagree on whether regular BuckMe balances survive.

activities.spoilerFreeDescription: Deposit cash into BuckMe and put money into Family Savings. Cash in your pocket and in the house stash won't carry past the end of this chapter.
activities.whyNow: Guides recommend moving at least $5,000 into Family Savings before the chapter's final missions.

activities.title: Down to Earth
activities.spoilerFreeDescription: Afterwards, a quiet at-home moment becomes available the next morning.
activities.whyNow: Unlocks the chapter's most important missable. Don't advance past it without doing it.

activities.title: A quiet morning at home

missable.latestSafe: Before starting Tourist Trap (Recalibration is the last call)
missable.earliest: The morning after Down to Earth
missable.warning: Permanently missable at the end of Chapter 1, and possibly required for the Positive Mental Attitude trophy. Do it the morning after Down to Earth.

activities.spoilerFreeDescription: One morning soon, Lucia offers a quiet moment at home. Say yes. It's the only chance in this chapter, and it may count toward a trophy.
activities.whyNow: The guide's top missable. It costs two minutes.
hints: An at-home moment with Lucia appears one morning soon. Accept it when it's offered.
Morning, in the kitchen, after Down to Earth.

tips.title: Take a long gun into missions on purpose
tips.summary: Owned long guns don't follow you around. You carry only what's in your loadout, and the rest waits in a car trunk or a weapon locker. Before anything that could turn into a firefight, open the trunk and take one.
points: Your active loadout holds up to two sidearms and two long guns. Owning more guns doesn't add slots.
At an open trunk, hold L1 (PS5) or LB (Xbox) to open the loadout and swap guns in or out. On PS5, Square stows a long gun. Guides disagree on the Xbox face buttons, so follow the prompt on screen.

Around town, carry one long gun at most, on your back, and leave the rest in the trunk. Take a second one only when you're heading into a fight. Two guides say a second long gun has to be carried in your hands, which makes people scatter and can get the police asking questions.
Sidearms holster out of sight, but long guns can't. A visible long gun is one of the things police use to identify you, so put it back in the trunk after a job.
Trunk and weapon-locker loadouts open up once you finish the Chapter 1 trip to the gun store.
Keep them in Jason's own car in Chapter 1. Two guides say what's in its trunk survives death or arrest, and once you can call for it, it's brought to you.
Output Lag says skipping the long gun purchase at the gun store can hold up a later story call.

nudge.text: If this could turn into a fight, check your trunk first. Your long guns stay there unless you take them.

tips.notes: Carry rules vary between guides: games.gg and XboxPlay give two sidearms and two long guns, while GamerBlurb describes one gun of each type. Only XboxPlay (and a pre-release GTABase preview) says the second long gun must be held in hand. Guides also disagree on whether a gun stored in one car can be taken from another car's trunk (GamerBlurb yes, DTG Reviews says check the car you stored it in). No guide lists which missions take your weapons away or hand you a loadout. Output Lag (Nov 22) also gives two sidearms and two long guns. Thumb Wars says long guns stay in the car you stored them in, which fits DTG Reviews.

tips.title: Buy the guns you want to keep
tips.summary: Guns you buy are yours for good. Drop one, die or get busted and you can take it back out of a weapon locker or your car's trunk. Guns picked up from enemies are only borrowed.
points: Picked-up guns are lost if you drop them, die or get busted, and along with any car they're stored in if it's destroyed or abandoned.
One guide says the loadout marks owned guns light blue, picked-up guns white and unique variants gold.
One guide says bought guns are shared between Jason and Lucia.
tips.notes: Icon colours come from DTG Reviews only; the shared arsenal from NoobFeed only. DTG Reviews says picked-up guns kept in a trunk survive saving and reloading, but loading an older save can undo later storage.

tips.title: Weapon lockers hold the rest of your arsenal

points: Not every Ammu-Nation has a locker. Check the shop on the map before you drive over.
At the locker you can equip a gun or send it to your car's trunk.
One guide reports a bug where a gun shows as in the trunk but can't be taken out. Take it from a locker instead.
tips.notes: GamerBlurb says lockers and trunks share one stored inventory, so you don't have to go back to where you left a gun; DTG Reviews says to check the car you actually stored it in. NoobFeed says certain garages have lockers; Red Bull says garages give loadout access.

points: With a sight fitted, click the right stick to aim in first person. Iron sights don't allow it.
When police response is the problem, a suppressor helps more than a damage upgrade.
One guide says the Key Lento Ammu-Nation sells a cheap suppressor right after the opening.
Police also come more slowly to gunfire near gang hideouts.
tips.notes: The Key Lento suppressor and the gang-hideout detail come from Red Bull only.

tips.title: Thin out a group with takedowns first
tips.summary: Money and ammo are scarce early on. Crouch, get behind lone guards and take them down quietly before any shooting starts.
points: Crouch with Circle (PS5) or B (Xbox). Moving slowly makes less noise.
Behind an unaware enemy, hold R2 or RT to grab, then keep tapping Square or X. A single tap won't finish it.
Pick off guards on the edges first, especially anyone alone or facing away. Tall grass and dark alleys hide your approach.
If someone turns or starts to notice you, break line of sight and get to cover. Takedowns only work from behind.
tips.notes: GTABase and NoobFeed give the same hold-then-tap input. Game-Checklists says players report that non-lethal takedowns push your criminal profile toward Professional.

tips.title: Fight from cover, in short bursts
tips.summary: Enemies spread out, take cover and flank. Stay behind something solid, fire in short bursts and keep out of tight rooms.
points: Press R1 (PS5) or RB (Xbox) to take cover, and again to leave it. Press X or A to round a corner without leaving cover.
Fire from cover with R2 or RT, then duck back. Held fire spreads, so shoot in short bursts.
Press Left on the D-pad while aiming to swap shoulders. Triangle or Y swaps weapons, which can be quicker than reloading.
Once you can switch characters, your partner can flank or give covering fire.
tips.notes: Controls are from GTABase; NoobFeed, Game-Checklists and GamerBolt agree on the cover and flanking advice.

tips.title: Throw something to split guards up
tips.summary: Pull one guard away from the group before you move in. A thrown bottle draws enemies toward the noise.
points: Pick up something like a glass bottle and throw it with R2 or RT.
GTABase says holding L2 or LT while looking at an enemy whistles them over to you.
Focus shows nearby enemies and things you can throw.
tips.notes: GTABase only.

tips.title: Counter instead of trading punches
tips.summary: Hold X (PS5) or A (Xbox) to block, and press it just before a punch lands to counter, then hit back. Every swing costs stamina.
points: Square or X attacks; hold it for a heavy hit.
Hold R2 or RT to grapple, then press Square or X to follow up.
With your stamina empty, your hits are weaker until it recovers.
tips.notes: GTABase only.

tips.title: Police only come when someone reports you
tips.summary: Cops respond when a witness, an alarm or a tracked stolen car calls it in. Check who can see you before you act, and leave before the responding units arrive.
points: Hollow stars: a crime was reported, but they don't know who did it.
Solid white stars: they're chasing you and know who you are.
Flashing stars: they've lost sight of you and are searching.
Red stars: they've left, but the area is still hot.
Witnesses can report threatening behaviour, so keep weapons out of sight.
Press L1 (PS5) or LB (Xbox) to holster before you walk into a crowd, and again to draw. A drawn gun gets bystanders calling it in.

tips.title: Clear the six things the police know about you
tips.summary: Heat comes from your face, your outfit, a visible weapon, your vehicle, camera footage and your partner. Deal with each one and the search fizzles out.
points: Face: wear a hat and bandana or a mask during the crime and take them off once you're out of sight. Hats, glasses and bandanas are on the item wheel.
Outfit: keep a spare outfit in your own car's trunk. Output Lag says it holds up to five.
Weapon: holster sidearms and stow long guns in the trunk.
Vehicle: ditch it, swap it or get it repainted at a Pay 'n' Spray.
Cameras: destroy the footage in the back room before you leave.
Partner: split Jason and Lucia up.
Change clothes and cars only after you've broken line of sight. Doing it in front of an officer won't help.
tips.notes: GTABase says cloud CCTV can't be wiped, only on-site footage, and that Pay 'n' Spray may refuse some cars depending on their tracker. Bloodstains and exploded dye packs also help police recognise you (GTABase).

tips.title: Break line of sight, then leave the search area
tips.summary: Get out of view first, then out of the marked search area. Don't drive back into the red heat zone until it fades.
points: Side streets, alleys and buildings break line of sight faster than open roads. In the countryside, woods and bushes work.
In a parked car, hold Circle (PS5) or B (Xbox) to duck behind the wheel and let patrols pass.
Use Focus to see where officers are. One guide says they don't show on the minimap.
Shoot out tyres to spin pursuers out. Helicopters back off after enough hits.
During robberies, a fast sports bike cuts through traffic and out of the search area.
One guide's escape from helicopter chases at four stars and up: follow the train tracks, where police cars rarely spawn.
Ladders, rooftops and unlocked doors are good places to hide. If K9 units are called in, keep moving, because the dogs track you.
Players report driving off a bridge into water as a quick escape: cars don't explode and the police lose sight of you.
tips.notes: Guides disagree on six stars: Red Bull says the only way out is being busted or wasted, while KeenGamer gives escape steps. The train-track route and sports bike are PowerPyx only. GTABase's combat guide confirms ducking in a parked car. The bridge escape comes from player reports collected by Game-Checklists.

tips.title: Your criminal profile can't always be undone
tips.summary: How violently you play sets a criminal profile, and it changes how your partner behaves when you're not controlling them. The worst level is permanent.
points: There are five levels: Professional, Hardened, Violent, Psycho and Irredeemable. Your kill count drives it most.
Irredeemable can't be reversed.
Head and chest shots kill; arm and leg shots injure. A yellow hit marker means injured, red means dead.
Killing police makes them come down harder and pushes your profile toward Violent.
Professional earns Focus from non-lethal takedowns; Violent and Psycho earn it from headshots.
Takedowns, limb shots and a suppressor keep you at Professional. Killing civilians, police or animals drags you down.
From Psycho on, you can't surrender, Output Lag says. Keep an older save if you're experimenting.
tips.notes: Red Bull and NoobFeed describe the five levels and the permanent Irredeemable level; GTABase confirms the shift toward Violent. The Focus detail is Red Bull only. Guides also say criminal profile is one of the reported ending factors (see research gaps). Output Lag, MovieWeb and Game-Checklists (Nov 20 to 22) agree that Irredeemable sticks unless you load an older save.

tips.title: From two stars, watch for tasers
tips.summary: At two stars and up, officers come at you with tasers from several sides. One hit empties your stamina and lets two of them cuff you.
points: Keep moving and don't let them box you in. More stamina gives you a chance to break free.
tips.notes: Game-Checklists, compiled from player reports.

tips.title: Deposit your cash after every job
tips.summary: Dying or getting busted costs you the cash and loot bags you carry. Bank cash at an ATM as soon as you can.
points: The banking app shows the nearest ATM. Deposits need a real ATM; you can't pay cash in from the phone.
Before you have a bank account, hide cash under the loose floorboards in Jason's bedroom. It takes deposits any time.
You can't carry more than $20,000 in cash. Anything over that stays where it is.
Shops take at most $999 in cash. Bigger purchases come out of your account, which PowerPyx puts at anything over $1,000.
Getting busted or wasted also costs a small banking fee, one guide says.
Mission pay often goes to the mailbox or the stash instead of your pocket.
tips.notes: Output Lag and Game-Checklists say you lose all the cash you carry when you die or get busted; GamerBolt says some of it, Inven Global calls it a risk. The $20,000 limit is MovieWeb and Inven Global; the $999 shop limit Output Lag only; the banking fee GTABase only. PowerPyx says money put into Family Savings can't be taken back out, and Output Lag agrees (see the research gap on what survives Chapter 1).

tips.title: Don't grind money early
tips.summary: The early story isn't kind to big piles of cash, and better ways to earn open up later. Spend on guns and car upgrades instead of saving up.
points: One guide says you lose most of your cash to story events in roughly the first third of the game.
Registering and selling stolen cars opens in Chapter 2, and better jobs and buyers in Chapter 3.
The journal still flags the few moments when you need money ready.
tips.notes: Guides disagree on early robberies: Red Bull says you can rob almost anywhere from the start, while PowerPyx says early money comes from gang operations and most store robberies open from the middle of Chapter 3.

tips.title: Sell loot to the fence who pays most for it
tips.summary: Stolen goods come in three kinds: narcotics, jewellery and marked bills. Different fences pay better for different kinds, and better fences unlock as the story goes on.
points: Two fences you meet later pay best: one for jewellery and marked bills, one for narcotics.
Later, fences offer to collect loot from you for a fee.
tips.notes: The pick-up service is Red Bull only. GamerBlurb names two earlier buyers before these.

tips.title: Check the mailbox outside Jason's house
tips.summary: Mission pay and money from your contacts often goes to the mailbox outside the house, not into your pocket.
tips.notes: Output Lag only. Jason's house is left behind at the end of Chapter 1.

tips.title: Treasure dives are safe early money
tips.summary: Kenton's dives come with no police and pay on the spot. Output Lag calls them the safest early money.
points: Dive sites show as purple chest icons. The boat at the dock behind Jason's house will get you there.
Focus highlights floating packages near wrecks.
Output Lag says the first wreck should pay about $1,400.

nudge.text: No police on these, and Kenton pays on the spot. Use Focus to spot floating packages near the wreck.

tips.notes: games.gg lists treasure diving as an early earner and Thumb Wars mentions shipwreck dives; the icons, Focus and payout are Output Lag only.

tips.title: Scout a robbery before you start it
tips.summary: Check the security rating on the map, find the back door, note the cameras and park a getaway car with room for loot. Medium and high security jobs are far easier with both characters.
points: Low security is fine solo. For medium and high, invite your partner from the map icon: Triangle (PS5) or Y (Xbox).
A Snap Gun opens back doors without tripping the alarm.
Safe codes are sometimes written nearby, and Focus highlights them. Codes change every game. Other safes need a tool or sticky bombs.
Use a different escape car from the one you arrive in, and decide in advance where you'll switch.
Finish one job and secure the loot before you start the next.

tips.title: Leave banks and loan stores for Chapter 3
tips.summary: Their cash comes with dye packs that explode if you get too far away. Chapter 3 gives you a tool that stops them.
tips.notes: Red Bull, NoobFeed and MovieWeb agree on dye packs and the Chapter 3 tool. GTABase separately confirms exploding dye packs. Laundering is games.gg only.
points: games.gg says money from banks can also need laundering before you can spend it.

tips.title: Know where your loot bags go
tips.summary: Each character carries two stash bags. Car trunks hold several, vans and trucks up to eight, and motorcycles none.
points: Bags you carry are lost if you die or get busted. Bags in a vehicle usually survive, unless it's destroyed or impounded.
Working as a pair, pass bags to your partner: Right on the D-pad, then Circle (PS5) or B (Xbox).
An impounded car shows under Personal on the map and can be recovered from the lot. One guide warns that a later remote-recovery service may return it without the bags.
tips.notes: The impound details come from DTG Reviews only.

tips.title: Switch off the alarm and wipe the footage
tips.summary: In a store robbery, the alarm panel is in the back room. Turn it off and nobody calls the police, then destroy the security footage so you can't be identified.
points: GTABase says on-site cameras can be destroyed, but footage already sent to the cloud can't, and trying sets the alarm off.
Output Lag says knocking the clerk out should also stop the call. games.gg warns some clerks are armed.
Threats don't hurt your criminal profile, GTABase says, but needless violence does.

tips.title: Bring a truck for wall ATMs
tips.summary: Some ATMs can be ripped off the wall and towed away, and you need a truck to do it. Towable ATMs show on the map.
points: Inven Global says an SUV takes more damage and carries more loot than a sports car.

tips.title: Scan a car before you steal it
tips.summary: Hold Up on the D-pad to open WAiNK and point it at a car. It shows the car's security, what it sells for and what registering it costs.
points: An alarm alerts people nearby when you smash a window.
A standard tracker stops you modding the car until it's registered.
An advanced tracker pings the police if the car gets too far from where you took it. Drive fast enough and the pings stop. Avoid these early on.
Most cars can be hotwired. High-end keyless cars need a key cloner, which comes later.
Scans count toward 100%.

tips.title: Register stolen cars to keep them
tips.summary: From Chapter 2 you can register stolen cars at a Pay 'n' Spray, and cheaper cars cost less to register. Registered cars can be called to you with the Scooter Bros app.
points: Garage space is tight at first. Register one everyday car and expand when you can afford it.
Bought garages store cars for free, give loadout access and let you drop off goods for others to sell. One guide suggests buying them only after you leave Key Lento.
Scan the car with WAiNK first. It shows whether it has a tracker, what it sells for and what it costs to register, which Output Lag puts at several times its sale value.
You need a free garage or parking space. Output Lag says garages are bought through the Vice City Real Estate app after a later Chapter 2 story mission.
tips.notes: Garage capacity advice is GamerBlurb only; the garage perks and timing are Red Bull only.

tips.title: Watch your fuel, and reload to repair
tips.summary: Every vehicle needs fuel, aircraft included, and damage adds up. Gas stations fix light damage, a mod shop or Pay 'n' Spray the rest.
points: Check the fuel gauge before a long trip into the swamps or out to the islands.
PowerPyx says a manual save and reload repairs your car for free. In Chapter 1 it also puts you back at the house.
Inven Global says the Scooter Bros app delivers a repaired car to you for a fee, with a few free deliveries a day on its premium plan.
Aircraft respawn in the same spots, so stealing another is a quick refill.
tips.notes: Fuel: PowerPyx, Inven Global and GamerBolt. Gas-station repairs: GamerBlurb and Inven Global. The reload repair and aircraft respawns are PowerPyx only; the Scooter Bros plan Inven Global only.

tips.title: Keep Jason's own car close
tips.summary: In Chapter 1, Jason's own car is your safe trunk. What's in it survives death or arrest, and once you can call the mechanic, it's brought to you repaired, even if it sank.
points: After the story mission that introduces the mechanic, call him from your contacts. Output Lag says delivery is free.
Its trunk holds long guns, loot bags and spare outfits.
Other stolen cars disappear when you die, get busted or leave them. Parking one at the house doesn't keep it.
Output Lag warns that upgrading the car before that mission can hide the repair you need there, and that the colour you pick then is your only free respray.
Personal vehicles don't carry past the end of Chapter 1. After that, register a car to keep it.
tips.notes: Output Lag and Game-Checklists agree on the trunk and the free delivery. Thumb Wars says to keep long guns in Jason's car. The upgrade warning is Output Lag only.

tips.title: Swing the car door at chasers
tips.summary: While driving, press Square (PS5) or X (Xbox) to fling your door open. It knocks bikers off and stops people dragging you out.

tips.title: Pay to skip the ride
tips.summary: There's no map warp, but a RydeMe car or a taxi lets you pay about $100 extra to skip the trip. Buses and trains are cheaper and run on schedules.
points: PowerPyx: get in, look at the driver (L2 or LT) and hold Triangle or Y to pay. Unexplored areas cost more the farther away they are.
A train line covers the whole region.
Inven Global says tipping the driver $5, up to twice, makes them drive faster.
Paradise Taxi is in your contacts. Output Lag says a cab may not reach you on a small island, so get to the mainland or a bridge first.
tips.notes: When RydeMe unlocks is disputed (see the research gap on unlock timing); PowerPyx lists it after Chapter 2.

tips.title: Finish Key Lento before you move on
tips.summary: The first stretch of the game is in Key Lento, and driving back later takes about ten minutes. Do the treasure dives, fishing and the neighbour's favours while you're there.
points: Some of it is lost for good at the end of Chapter 1. Check the Missables tab before the chapter's last mission.
Explore the bars and the full interiors while you're there.
tips.notes: Red Bull and NoobFeed may share a source. The Chapter 1 missables come from the guide's own checked steps.

tips.title: Fly to clear the map fog
tips.summary: One guide's fastest way to uncover the whole map: take a taxi to a plane and fly over everything. It takes about two to three hours.

tips.title: Let the game drive
tips.summary: Hold Down on the D-pad for the cinematic camera and follow the prompt. Your character drives to the waypoint on their own and obeys traffic.
points: It crawls in heavy traffic, so pay for a ride when time matters.
Settings > Accessibility > Auto Drive: Restricted keeps it out of risky moves. Unrestricted can cause crashes.
Game-Checklists says it works in boats too.
tips.notes: Thumb Wars says holding Down slows time and highlights nearby shops and missions instead, so the input may depend on whether you're driving.

tips.title: Switch characters instead of driving
tips.summary: Switching to your other character is the quickest and cheapest way across the map. Whoever you're not playing usually waits near the current safehouse.
tips.notes: KeenGamer and Output Lag name one Chapter 2 story mission; Beebom (Nov 22) says the next one. The safehouse restriction is Beebom only.
points: Hold Right on the D-pad to open the partner menu, then press R1 (PS5) or RB (Xbox). A quick tap of Right sets off placed explosives instead.
If you're together the swap is instant. If not, the camera pulls out across the map to wherever your partner is.
Free switching opens in Chapter 2. Two guides name one story mission, one says the mission after it.
Story missions and J or L map markers can lock you to one character. One guide says you can't switch inside a safehouse either.

tips.title: Hold Right on the D-pad for your partner
tips.summary: The partner menu does more than switch. Call your partner over, hand them the wheel, or split up.
points: Hold Right, then press Triangle (PS5) or Y (Xbox), to bring your partner to you or split up.
Set a waypoint, start driving, then switch to the passenger seat and your partner drives you there. In a chase, one drives while the other shoots.
Inven Global says you can also ask them to distract the police, or to sell your loot for a little less than you'd get yourself.
tips.notes: The police and loot-selling orders are Inven Global only, from a pre-release review build.

tips.title: They don't share ammo or meds
tips.summary: A gun either of them buys is available to both, but ammo, healing items and weapon mods are separate. Stock up each one before a job.
tips.notes: Inven Global played a pre-release review build and GamerBolt cites early reports; Output Lag says owned guns should be shared. Whether training together counts for both is disputed (see the training tip).

tips.title: Train Health, Stamina and Focus differently
tips.summary: Lifting raises Health, cardio raises Stamina, and calm pastimes like fishing and pool raise Focus. Health and Stamina fade if you stop training, but Focus gains are permanent.
points: On the weights, press both triggers in quickly and let them out slowly. Finish the set before your stamina runs out.
Stop when the ring in the fitness app closes, then have a protein bar or shake.
The weights are outside Jason's house. A gym membership adds treadmills and bikes, but there's no gym in the starting area.
Shooting ranges and crazy golf also raise Focus. PowerPyx says the Market Range at Rodgers Ranch & Shooting Range can be repeated for max Focus.
Training both characters together counts for both, one guide says.
Strength and cardio gains are capped each day, so a short session daily beats one long one. Focus has no cap.
Output Lag says a protein shake from the fridge halves the wait before you can train again; Game-Checklists says players report the same from protein bars.
Inven Global says gym membership opens in Chapter 3, and the Health app on your phone shows your stats.
tips.notes: Training both characters together counts for both, Red Bull says; Output Lag says each one trains separately. The daily cap is Output Lag and Game-Checklists.

tips.title: Eat, sleep and shower for buffs
tips.summary: Eating, sleeping and showering give buffs that last until you die or quit. Skipping food and sleep costs you stats.
points: A good routine: sleep at night, work out in the morning, then eat and shower.
Overeating can make your character gain weight.
Showering at a safehouse also washes off blood that helps police recognise you.
Feeding Jason's snake gives a small Focus buff, one guide says.
tips.notes: The snake buff is Red Bull only; the shower and blood detail GTABase only.

tips.title: Use Focus to search, not just to shoot
tips.summary: Click both sticks for Focus. In a fight it slows time; outside one it lasts as long as you like and highlights enemies in red, usable things in yellow and cash in green.
points: It shows enemies through walls, notes with safe codes, animal tracks and valuables in car trunks.
Doors show white if you can go in and red if they're alarmed.
It also points you toward nearby voices and sounds, which leads to random encounters and hidden stashes.
In a fight, red marks lethal spots and yellow non-lethal ones.

nudge.text: Click both sticks to hear where voices and sounds are coming from.

tips.title: Heal from the item wheel
tips.summary: Hold L1 and press Square (LB and X on Xbox) for Zombix, which restores half your health, or L1 and Triangle (LB and Y) for adrenaline, a bigger boost.

tips.title: Fish to build Focus
tips.summary: Focus is the slowest stat to raise, and fishing is the quickest way to grow it. You can fish as soon as you're free to roam, from the dock behind Jason's house.
points: Near water, hold L1 (PS5) or LB (Xbox), open the Equipment tab and choose the rod.
Hold L2 or LT and press R2 or RT to cast. When a fish bites, let it take the bait, then press R2 or RT to hook it.
Pull the left stick against the way the fish swims, and turn the right stick to reel in when it pauses. Settings > Accessibility > Fishing: Hold replaces the stick turning.
It's catch and release, so there's nothing to sell. Game-Checklists says each catch gives about 10 Focus.
Better lures are sold at Chuck's Tackle & Shot in Key Lento.

nudge.text: Every catch also raises Focus, the slowest stat to train.

tips.notes: Controls are from Shacknews, written from a pre-release build. The Focus figure is Game-Checklists only.

tips.title: Study animals from a distance
tips.summary: Hold R1 (PS5) or RB (Xbox) to study an animal, or use binoculars so you don't scare it off. Some look-alikes are rare species.

nudge.text: Use binoculars so you don't spook it, and study look-alikes too. Some are rare species.

tips.title: Talk to locals for leads
tips.summary: People around Leonida hand out leads on side jobs and stick-ups. Some ask for help and some turn hostile.
points: Game-Checklists says tipping locals gets you leads on stick-up spots.

tips.title: Keep one manual save per chapter
tips.summary: Save from Pause, then Game, then Save. Main missions can't be freely replayed and each chapter's safehouse is left behind, so an older save is your only way back.
points: You can't save during the Prologue. Finish it in one sitting and save as soon as it unlocks.
Autosave only happens when a mission ends, and you can't save mid-mission.
There are 15 manual slots. Use a new one at the start of each chapter and before its last mission.
There's no mission replay, even after the credits.

tips.title: Check the time before you head out
tips.summary: Press Up on the D-pad to see the clock on your phone. Some shops close at night and some missions only run at certain hours. Sleeping at home moves the clock on.
points: Nights are very dark. Settings > Display > Brightness Calibration helps.
tips.notes: Opening hours and mission times are Red Bull only; the brightness setting PowerPyx only.

tips.title: Read the map's colours
tips.summary: On the world map, dark blue buildings have interiors you can enter and light blue ones are scenery. Near an enterable building, the minimap marks the entrance with a white line.
points: Main missions show as pink bubbles with black letters, optional ones as black bubbles with pink letters, and small side tasks as purple icons.
Filter the map with Down, then Right on the D-pad.
Inside shops, the minimap shows hidden rooms, staircases and back doors.
tips.notes: Building colours: Red Bull and MovieWeb, and GamerBolt mentions map shading. Shop minimaps are Red Bull only; marker colours and filters PowerPyx only.

nudge.text: Dark blue buildings on the map can be entered, sometimes through a vent or window.

tips.title: Turn on every notification
tips.summary: Switching on all UI notifications helps you track collectibles and changes to your criminal profile.

tips.title: Check your phone's Reminders before leaving an area
tips.summary: The Reminders section lists messages, people to call and new opportunities, so it's a quick check that you haven't left anything behind.

tips.title: Change a few settings before you start
tips.summary: Turn subtitles fully on, lower motion blur and set movement to run on a full stick push. Aim and camera numbers are personal, so treat any guide's values as a starting point.
points: Audio > Subtitles: change Mission Only to On before the opening mission.
Display > Motion Blur Strength: 0 for the sharpest image, or low if 30 fps feels choppy. Every console runs at 30 fps with no performance mode.
Gameplay > Movement Speed: Run or Jog, so a full push of the stick runs without clicking it. Guides disagree on which.
Gameplay > Targeting: Partial is the default and a good start. Free Aim still locks on up close unless you also turn off Shooting Assist.
Camera Shake off, and turn down the crash and kill cameras if they break up chases and fights.
UI > Navigation: Always On keeps the minimap visible during chases. One guide prefers Dynamic for a cleaner screen.

nudge.text: While you're in Settings: subtitles fully on, motion blur down, movement set to run.

tips.notes: Guides disagree on aim assist strength (0 to 4 or 0 to 5), movement speed, camera height and camera bob.

tips.title: No difficulty setting, but there are assists
tips.summary: Settings > Gameplay has Accessible Combat, Reduced Vehicle Damage and Simplified Mini Games. They're off by default, and you can switch them on for one hard mission and off again.
points: Accessible Combat means you take less damage and enemies take more.
Simplified Mini Games makes the gym, basketball and hot-wiring inputs easier.
MovieWeb says they don't affect trophies or achievements.
tips.notes: PowerPyx suggests saving them for a mission you're stuck on or post-story cleanup.

tips.title: Unique weapons are yours for good
tips.summary: Unique weapon variants show up yellow in the world and in menus. Once Jason or Lucia picks one up, it's unlocked for both, and you can take it back out of any weapon locker if you lose it.
points: Some are sold rather than hidden: a few gun stores stock variants you won't find anywhere else.
One guide says variants can't be modified, so don't plan on fitting a suppressor to one.
Pickups inside story missions are the exception. Take them during the mission, because you can't go back for them.

researchGaps.detail: Mission order, unlocks and what's lost at Starting From Zero are the least documented parts of the game. Dork's late chapters were still being filled in.
Only 4 of the 8 qualifying strands are confirmed (Kirk, Kyle, Yago, Pilot Pete). Bret, Randy, Dunk and Kenton are unstated.

researchGaps.area: Balcony meditation and Positive Mental Attitude
researchGaps.detail: Whether the Chapter 1 balcony meditation is strictly required for the trophy is disputed.
Guides disagree on whether trusting or not trusting him at the motel unlocks part 3. The Vapid 32 Hustler reward is single-source.
English guides say Power Play closes it; one Polish guide says it isn't time-limited. Needs an in-game test.
Exact expiry for Race Against Yago and the Shayna pickup is undocumented, as is whether sleeping advances the timer.
WAiNK (Unwanted Attention vs Moses), RydeMe (Buck Me vs after Chapter 2), large bank vaults (end of Chapter 4 vs Chapter 5).

Sources disagree on whether regular BuckMe balances survive Tourist Trap or only Family Savings (up to $5,000). PowerPyx's tips page adds that money put into Family Savings can't be taken back out, though it raises your checking-account limit. Output Lag (Nov 22) says pocket cash, the floor stash and the main BuckMe balance don't carry into Chapter 2, bought guns do, and Family Savings should carry over but can't be withdrawn. MovieWeb also says to spend Chapter 1 money or turn it into guns.

The Weapons checklist has 122 of the 127 variants Detonated counts, plus its 2 Ultimate Edition extras. 25 have no known location. Most rows rest on Detonated alone. Guides disagree on where two are: the dish-covered trailer and the motel south of Hamlet. Whether the Kalaga Reservoir pistol is a unique variant is single-source.
An abandoned research facility behind keypad code 2314 is reported with no confirmed location. Wyman's Classic Car Collection (car-hunt commission) has no documented trigger, count or locations.
Per-chapter card maps, meteorite totals and gold-doubloon totals aren't published. WAiNK location totals conflict (31 vs 112 listed; 100 required).
Collect Moses' Gift, Steal the Scooter, Gone Fishing trailer cash amount, Mandy's cigar use and the Shayna pickup reward are undocumented.
Beyond the wounded hunter and the jet-ski dog, random-event lists weren't verified for this version.
Reported factors are choices, relationship, criminal profiles and money invested. The number of endings and the weight of each factor aren't confirmed.

Most guides now give two sidearms and two long guns (GamerBlurb says one per type). Still unclear: whether the second long gun has to be held in hand, and whether a gun stored in one car's trunk can be taken from another car (Thumb Wars and DTG Reviews say no). Xbox trunk buttons also differ between guides.
KeenGamer and Output Lag say free switching between Jason and Lucia opens after one Chapter 2 story mission; Beebom says after the next one.

researchGaps.area: Fights in a few story missions
researchGaps.detail: 3 story missions, all in Chapter 4, aren't described well enough by any guide to say whether they involve a fight. IGN's walkthrough covers the Prologue to Chapter 3 so far, so most Chapter 4 and 5 fight ratings still rest on one walkthrough.

researchGaps.area: Main missions missing from the guide
researchGaps.detail: IGN's walkthrough lists one more main mission in Chapter 2 and one in Chapter 3 that this guide doesn't have yet.

changelog.note: First version. Built from the three project research documents, cross-checked against launch-week guides (PowerPyx, Dork, Game-Checklists, FinalBoss, Output Lag, GTABase, WikiGTAVI).
Removed the three 'save before a choice' checklist items. They're warnings, not tasks, so they now show as a save reminder on the mission that holds the choice.
Added this work-in-progress card with a coverage strip, so you can see which chapters are well covered and which are still thin.

New Tips tab: 31 tips from ten launch guides, from when to take a long gun into a mission to shaking the police, banking cash and training. Story missions now remind you to check your trunk, and Ask the guide answers from the tips too.

19 more tips from eleven new guides: combat and stealth, Jason and Lucia, settings, fishing and safe early money. The Now tab is simpler: Keep in mind picks three tips for where you are (hide the ones you know), and pace sits next to Also open.

Story missions now carry a fight rating from the walkthroughs: gunfight, maybe some shooting, fists only or no fighting. Next up and Before you advance say when to grab a long gun from the trunk. Three Chapter 4 missions aren't rated yet.

Checked every fight rating from the Prologue to Chapter 3 against IGN's walkthrough. Most now have two guides behind them, and a few changed: one Chapter 1 mission turns out to have a shootout. Chapters 4 and 5 wait for IGN's coverage.

Spoiler pass: fight ratings now show only for your next story mission, with loadout notes instead of mission details. Tips no longer name later missions or characters, and the research gaps list is folded away.

New in the Journal: a Unique weapons filter that lists every place the guide knows with one, across all chapters. Two newer guides confirmed most of them and added four. Guides count 127 variants; most gun-store and robbery ones aren't listed yet.

New Weapons tab: a checklist of every unique weapon variant guides have named so far, 122 plus 2 Ultimate Edition extras, grouped by type. Names stay hidden until you open a row. 25 haven't been located by anyone yet, and most rows rest on one guide.
